top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a single, concrete invention: a magic-wavelength lattice cancels Doppler and recoil shifts while many atoms are interrogated at once, taking fractional uncertainty to about 1e-18, reproduced independently in Sr, Yb and Hg. It is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, and the two-name allocation (Katori for the concept and first demonstrations, Ye for record accuracy and many-body-enhanced operation) captures the decisive credit, with a citation confined to the lattice clock. It is mature and clearly preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for the lattice clock (Katori, Ye); my electron-microscopy field proximity applies only to B009, which is not on the slate
